Deep dives / Americas

THE SPREAD OF PEOPLES · DEEP DIVE

Mesoamerican & North American Origin Stories: Aztec Five Suns, Maya Popol Vuh, Diné Emergence & Turtle Island

Here we step outside archaeological stratigraphy into living Indigenous scriptures and oral literature—exploring how Aztecs (Mexica/Nahua), K'iche' Maya, Diné (Navajo), Hopi, Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe, Haida/Tlingit, and Inuit storytellers explained the creation of Earth, sacred order, and the human family.

Primary sacred narratives and ethnographic texts across Central Mexico, the Guatemalan Maya Highlands, the US Southwest, the Eastern Woodlands / Great Lakes, the Northwest Coast, and the Arctic.

1. The Aztec (Mexica/Nahua) Five Suns, Quetzalcoatl in Mictlan & Aztlán

Recorded in sixteenth-century Nahuatl manuscripts (*Leyenda de los Soles*, *Histoyre du Mechique*, *Florentine Codex*) and carved into the monumental basalt Sun Stone (*Piedra del Sol*), Mexica origin cosmology unfolds across five fragile cosmic ages. Out of dual supreme principle **Ometeotl** (*Ometecuhtli / Omecihuatl* in Omeyocan), four creator brothers—**Xipe Totec**, **Tezcatlipoca**, **Quetzalcoatl**, and **Huitzilopochtli**—tore primeval earth-monster **Cipactli** apart to form land and sky, cycling through four earlier doomed Suns: Earth/Jaguar (*4 Jaguar*), Wind/Monkeys (*4 Wind*), Rain/Turkeys (*4 Rain*), and Water/Fish (*4 Water*) before Chalchiuhtlicue's great flood washed away humanity. [1] [2]

At the ruined sacred darkness of **Teotihuacan**, the gods gathered around a roaring hearth to create the **Fifth Sun (*Nahui Ollin* — Sun of Movement)**: proud rich **Tecuciztecatl** flinched four times at the flames, while humble scab-covered **Nanahuatzin** leaped boldly inside and rose radiant in the east—demanding blood from all deities to move across the heavens. Next, **Quetzalcoatl** braved **Mictlan** (the Underworld), bypassed **Mictlantecuhtli**'s jagged trials with worms boring his conch trumpet, gathered the bones of past ages (ground like maize flour in **Cihuacoatl**'s jade bowl and quickened with **Quetzalcoatl**'s own penitential blood), and transformed into an ant to fetch yellow maize kernels hidden inside **Tonacatepetl** (Sustenance Mountain), grounding Mexica historical migration from **Chicomoztoc** ('Seven Caves') and **Aztlan** into Lake Texcoco. [3] [2]

2. The K'iche' Maya Popol Vuh: Mud People, Wood People & True Humans of Maize

Preserved by K'iche' nobles in alphabetic transcription during the 1550s (*Chichicastenango Manuscript*), the **Popol Vuh** opens inside silent green-blue cosmic waters where **Tz'aqol**, **B'itol**, **Tepew**, and feathered serpent **Q'uq'umatz** ('Heart of Sky and Heart of Earth') meditate aloud, uttering '*Earth!*' so mountain peaks push up through clearing mists. Wanting creatures capable of speaking their makers' names and reckoning sacred days, the deities tried three times: silent animals failed to speak beyond cries and were assigned forests; wet **earth/mud humans** sagged, dissolved in rain, and had no heads to turn; carved **Tz'ite' wood dolls** walked and multiplied but lacked hearts, memory, or gratitude, until black resin rains and their own angry cooking pots, grinding stones (*metates*), and dogs overthrew them (leaving spider monkeys as forest remnants). [4]

Only after the Hero Twins **Hunahpu** and **Xbalanque** defeated the lords of **Xibalba** in the underworld ballcourt and cleared the heavens did four animal scouts—Fox, Coyote, Parrot, and Crow—reveal fertile split mountain **Paxil and Kayala**. On the fourth attempt, grandmother deity **Xmukane** ground **yellow and white maize ears nine times**, washing her hands in spring water to knead broth for human strength and shaping the first four true ancestors (**B'alam Ki'tze'**, **B'alam Aq'ab'**, **Mahuk'utah**, and **Iq'i B'alam**) plus their four wives—beings so piercingly intelligent their vision penetrated sky and bedrock until the Creators breathed a gentle mist over their eyes to calibrate mortal foresight. [4]

3. Emergence Cosmologies of the Southwest: Diné Bahaneʼ & Hopi Sipapu

Unlike Genesis creation *ex nihilo*, Southwestern nations remember humanity and spirits ascending upward through layered subterranean worlds. In **Diné (Navajo) *Diné Bahaneʼ***, Insect-Beings and First Spirits traversed the mist-shrouded **Black First World (*Ni'hodilqil*)**, quarreled in the **Blue Second World (*Ni'hodootl'izh*)** of Bird-People, entered the sunlit fertile valleys of the **Yellow Third World (*Ni'haltsoh*)** where **First Man (*Áłtsé Hastiin*)** and **First Woman (*Áłtsé Asdzáá*)** emerged inside red/white corn stalks—before Coyote's theft of Water Monster (*Tééhooltsódii*)'s infants unleashed a subterranean flood driving everyone upward inside a giant hollow reed (**Łóókáá'**) out into the glittering **Fourth/Fifth White World**, stabilized by sacred mountains (*Sisnaajiní, Tsoodził, Dook'o'oosłííd, Dibé Nitsaa*) and renewed through **Changing Woman (*Asdzáá Nádleehé*)**, who created the founding Diné clans from her rubbed epidermis mixed with white and yellow corn. [5] [6]

In parallel **Hopi** teachings, Creator **Tawa** and **Spider Grandmother (*Kókyangwúti*)** molded clay figures beneath the Earth, guiding faithful groups through three prior imperfect worlds (corrupted by arrogance and division) up a great bamboo/reed ladder out the **Sipapu**—the sacred emergence opening near the Little Colorado River confluence—where guardian **Másaw** assigned clans migration spirals across four quarters before settling the Third, Second, and First Mesas. [5]

4. Eastern Woodlands Turtle Island, Northwest Coast Raven & Inuit Sea Traditions

Across **Haudenosaunee (Iroquois)** and **Anishinaabe (Ojibwe)** Earth-Diver narratives, the primordial earth lay wholly submerged beneath waters populated by diving animals and birds while Sky-People lived above. In Haudenosaunee tradition, pregnant **Sky Woman (*Atahensik* / Mature Flower)** fell through the roots of the uprooted Celestial Tree; graceful water-birds cupped their wings to catch her and lowered her onto Giant **Turtle**'s carapace while Beaver, Loon, and Otter failed to reach ocean bottom—until tiny **Muskrat** gasped upward clutching a mud-clod in her paw, smeared and danced outward over the shell by Sky Woman into the continent still called **Turtle Island** (later balanced by her grandsons **Sapling** / Sky-Holder and **Flint**). Along Pacific Northwest fjords (**Haida** & **Tlingit**), restless trickster **Raven** lifted sunlight out from cedar nesting-boxes inside a wealthy elder's house and coaxed muffled, timid first human beings (*K'iid K'iyaas*) out from a tight white giant clamshell on **Rose Spit**, introducing clans across forested coastal inlets; high north in **Inuit** tradition, wronged young woman **Sedna / Nuliajuk** sank beneath sea-ice where her chopped fingers transformed into seals, walrus, and whales governing Arctic abundance through hunter reciprocity. [5] [6]
